entries.title: Stellar Nucleosynthesis
entries.text: Stellar nucleosynthesis accounts for the observed abundances of elements heavier than helium. In the cores of main-sequence stars, hydrogen is fused into helium via the proton-proton chain or, in more massive stars, the CNO cycle, whose rate depends steeply on core temperature.

entries.title: Constraints on Dark Matter Halos
entries.text: Rotation curves of spiral galaxies remain approximately flat well beyond the optical radius, a result that is difficult to reconcile with the distribution of luminous matter alone. The conventional interpretation invokes an extended halo of non-baryonic dark matter whose density profile declines roughly as the inverse square of radius. Numerical simulations, however, predict cuspy central profiles, whereas observations of low surface brightness galaxies frequently favour cored distributions. Proposed resolutions include feedback from supernovae, which redistributes baryons and flattens the inner potential, and alternative particle models such as self-interacting dark matter.

entries.title: The Quiet Ship
entries.text: The ship had been quiet for a long time. Mira walked down the hall and listened to the hum of the engines. Out the window, a red planet turned slowly in the dark.

entries.title: Signal From the Ice
entries.text: The signal came from under the ice. At first the crew thought it was a fault in the radio, but it kept coming back, three short beeps and one long one, every ten minutes. Jonas put on his suit and took the small drill out to the edge of the camp. The wind was cold and the sky was a pale green. When he cut through the last layer, a soft blue light rose up from the hole. Something down there was awake, and it had been waiting for them.

entries.title: Small Steps
entries.text: Start where you are and use what you have. A small step taken today is worth more than a perfect plan that never leaves the page. Progress is quiet; it rarely announces itself.

entries.title: On Practice
entries.text: Skill is just patience that has been repeated. The hands learn what the mind once struggled to hold, and one day the hard thing becomes the easy thing. Be kind to your early attempts; they are the reason your later ones will be good. Do not wait to feel ready, because readiness is usually something you notice afterwards. Measure your progress against yesterday, not against someone else's highlight reel.

entries.title: The Silk Roads
entries.text: The Silk Roads were never a single road. They were a shifting web of caravan routes linking China, Central Asia, Persia and the Mediterranean, carrying silk, spices, paper, and ideas across thousands of miles.

entries.title: The Printing Press
entries.text: When Johannes Gutenberg began printing with movable metal type around 1450, books were still rare and expensive. Within fifty years, presses had spread to more than two hundred European cities, and millions of volumes were in circulation. Pamphlets, calendars, and news sheets followed. Literacy rose, scholars could compare identical copies of a text, and arguments that once travelled slowly by hand could now cross a continent in weeks.

Top Customers
entries.text:
SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS orders, SUM(o.total) AS revenue
FROM customers AS c
JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.created_at >= DATE '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY c.name
HAVING SUM(o.total) > 1000
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 10;

entries.title: Monthly Retention
entries.text:
WITH first_orders AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at)) AS cohort
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
activity AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT o.customer_id, f.cohort,
         DATE_TRUNC('month', o.created_at) AS active_month
  FROM orders AS o
  JOIN first_orders AS f USING (customer_id)
)
SELECT cohort,
       active_month,
       COUNT(*) AS customers,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / FIRST_VALUE(COUNT(*)) OVER (
         PARTITION BY cohort ORDER BY active_month
       ), 1) AS pct_retained
FROM activity
GROUP BY cohort, active_month
ORDER BY cohort, active_month;
